name: Camera Sensor PRNU Identification
description: Identifies the source camera model or detects synthetic generation by analyzing the Photo-Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) sensor noise pattern and hardware processing pipeline fingerprints.
algorithm: Sensor PRNU Extraction and CFA Pattern Fingerprinting
mechanism: The algorithm extracts the high-frequency residual signal containing the device's unique Photo-Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) noise and traces of its Color Filter Array (CFA) interpolation pipeline. Authentic photographic images possess a consistent PRNU fingerprint tied to physical hardware silicon. AI-generated images lack this coherent physical signature, exhibiting either completely synthetic noise profiles, 'Frankenstein' amalgamations of multi-camera noise from training data, or physically impossible CFA demosaicing patterns.
parameters: Features: PRNU Correlation, CFA Demosaicing Map, Classifier: Cross-Correlation Filter / SVM, Window: 128x128 patches
accuracy: High (85-95%) - Extremely robust for identifying generic synthetic noise, though identifying the exact camera model requires a reference database.
source: Lukas, J. et al. (2006) - Digital Camera Identification from Sensor Pattern Noise
useCase: Verifying whether an image originated from real camera hardware, authenticating its claimed model, and exposing physically impossible sensor noise in AI generations.

references.title: Lukas, J. et al. (2006). Digital Camera Identification from Sensor Pattern Noise. IEEE TIFS.
Chen, M. et al. (2008). Determining Image Origin and Integrity Using Sensor Noise. IEEE TIFS.

strengths:
• Deeply anchored in physical semiconductor properties rather than semantic or visual content.
• Extracted PRNU acts as an intrinsic digital fingerprint that is practically impossible for AI to synthetically forge.
• Reliably distinguishes organic hardware sensor noise from the pseudo-random latent noise injected by diffusion models.
• Functions independently from lighting conditions, subject matter, or localized scene context.
limitations:
• Verifying an exact camera model demands an extensive reference library of pristine flat-field images.
• Substantially degraded by aggressive digital denoising filters, smartphone AI enhancement, or heavy JPEG quantization.
• Cannot distinguish between different interchangeable lenses mounted on the same physical camera sensor body.
• Scaling, rotation, or digital cropping inherently misaligns the PRNU map, disabling precise correlation.
